title: The Health Considerations When Switching from Smoking to Nicotine Pouches – Podtail
abstract:
## Are Nicotine Pouches Better For Health Than Smoking Cigarettes?  
In short, the answer is yes. However, as these products are still relatively new to the market, there is little data available, but studies are in progress. Moreover, the most important aspect to take not of is that nicotine pouches contain zero tobacco and tobacco is the main reason why cigarettes are so dangerous. It is the tobacco content (rather than the nicotine content) that is carcinogenic and contributes to heart and lung diseases. Furthermore, as nicotine pouches are non-combustible, there’s no wafting smoke, which means that there’s no risk of others inhaling second-hand smoke, as there is with smoking.  
It is worth noting that cigarettes contain free radicals, which attack the body, and another organ that faces significant damage due to cigarette smoke is the skin. Smoking causes it to age extremely quickly. This is because cigarettes cause the breakdown of elasticity and collagen, whereas nicotine pouches don’t affect the skin.
## Nicotine Pouches and Smoking Cessation  
As nicotine pouches don’t contain any tobacco and are smoke-free, more and more people are turning to these products to help them stop smoking. Again, studies are still in their infancy, but it is fair to say that similarly to nicotine patches, nicotine gum, nicotine sprays and nicotine lozenges, nicotine pouches are another product that can help smokers switch from traditional cigarettes. Also, unlike other smoking cessation products, nicotine pouches come in a selection of appealing flavours, which only enhances their appeal and makes them pleasurable to use. Many users of other smoking cessation products say that one of the reasons they fail to quit is because of the unpleasant flavour – as other products only come in limited flavours. In health terms, any product that helps a smoker to quit must be a benefit!
## Nicotine – The Many Lesser-Known Benefits  
Contrary to popular belief, it is not the nicotine that poses a danger in a lit cigarette, but the burning tobacco that’s inhaled into the lungs. Yes, doubtless, nicotine is an addictive substance, but it comes with far less health risks than tobacco and in fact, has some health benefits, listed as follows:  
- Nicotine (both synthetic and non-synthetic) is officially non-carcinogenic (does not cause cancer).
- Nicotine is an effective appetite-suppressant (good for weight control and reducing obesity).
- It has minimal effect on cardiovascular health.
- Studies say it may help prevent Alzheimer’s disease.
- Nicotine could prevent Parkinson’s disease.
- It may be able to treat ulcerative colitis.
- It is believed to help with cognitive function, especially in improving memory.
- It may be able to control ADHD (attention deficit disorder).
- It may be able to help control Tourette’s Syndrome.
- Clinical studies suggest that nicotine may reduce schizophrenic episodes.
- Nicotine is linked to reducing depression.
- Nicotine can prevent inflammation, therefore could also help control arthritis.
